## Tools

### `audit_agent_config`

Audit this project's agent configuration (.mcp.json, .claude/, .cursor/, .vscode/, .gemini/, plugin.json; user-level ones with include\_user\_config): unpinned npx/uvx servers, plain-http remote servers, inline secrets (redacted), wildcard Bash permissions, bypassPermissions, hooks that reach the network, ${VAR} placeholders Claude Code does not expand, entries changed since the last audit. Reads only; audit\_mcp\_tools inspects what servers serve.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | The project to audit. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `include_user_config` | boolean | no | `false` | Also read the user-level configs every project shares. Default false. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Response floor only; every finding is still recorded (`severity_filter`). |

### `audit_executive`

Run security\_scan\_full, quality\_check, deps\_audit and compliance\_check concurrently, plus the WordPress or .NET scans the latest detect\_stack calls for: one report — severity counts, top 10 findings, worst child coverage, change since the last audit. Egress: the Semgrep registry (with metrics), Trivy's database, npm, PyPI, NuGet feeds; Trivy's and Semgrep's version checks are off. Runs code: pip-audit's virtualenv, a .NET restore (MSBuild), the project's ESLint. local\_only keeps Semgrep local (`local_only_gaps`: what still went out).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Response floor only; every finding is still recorded (`severity_filter`). |
| `local_only` | boolean | no | — | Semgrep on disk only, no scan\_wordpress; the rest still goes out (`local_only_gaps`). |

### `audit_mcp_tools`

Start the MCP servers named in `servers` and check what they serve — tools, prompts, resources — for instructions aimed at the model, hidden Unicode, requests to read secrets or send data out, cross-server shadowing and oversized descriptions; a definition changed since the last audit is a high rug pull. This runs third-party code: only the servers the user named, with a minimal environment, never tools/call; remote ones only with allow\_remote. A failed server lowers coverage, never a clean pass.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | The project whose MCP configs declare them. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `servers` | array of string | yes | — | Config entry names to start and audit (e.g. \["github"\]), or `<source>::<name>`. No wildcard. |
| `include_user_config` | boolean | no | `false` | Also look the names up in the user-level configs. Default false. |
| `allow_remote` | boolean | no | `false` | Also start servers that reach another machine (url, ssh, kubectl, remote docker). Default false. |
| `timeout_ms` | number | no | `20000` | Per-server time budget, in ms. |

### `bug_hunt`

Semgrep bug hunt: p/r2c-bug-scan, p/security-audit and local packs (race conditions, null safety, off-by-one, leaks, error handling, edge cases) for JS/TS, Python, Go, Java, C# and PHP, plus register\_custom\_rules' rules. `categories` filters the response, not the scan. Pattern rules match syntax, not data flow: a quiet result is not bug-free. Local rules have no autofix: use suggest\_fix, not create\_fix\_pr. A pack that failed to load is reported, never a clean scan.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Response floor only; every finding is still recorded (`severity_filter`). |
| `auto_fix` | boolean | no | `false` | Apply Semgrep's autofixes to the source (a clean tree, unless allow\_dirty). |
| `allow_dirty` | boolean | no | `false` | With auto\_fix: allow uncommitted changes in the tree. |
| `categories` | array of string | no | — | Show only these bug subcategories (e.g. race\_condition); every finding is recorded. |
| `include_language_packs` | boolean | no | `false` | Also run the detected languages' Semgrep security packs (not bug classes). |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |
| `scope` | object | no | — | Scan part of the project: paths, a git change set, or changes since a ref or date. Never a baseline. |
| `scope.paths` | array of string | no | — | Files, directories or globs in project\_path; with diff or since, narrows that set. |
| `scope.diff` | object | no | — | A git change set. {} = every uncommitted change (staged, unstaged, untracked). |
| `scope.diff.base` | string | no | — | The files changed since the merge base of this ref and head. |
| `scope.diff.head` | string | no | — | Must be the checked-out commit. Default HEAD. |
| `scope.diff.staged` | boolean | no | — | Only the staged files. |
| `scope.diff.include_untracked` | boolean | no | — | Also untracked files. Default: true without base or staged. |
| `scope.since` | string | no | — | What changed since a commit, tag or date ("2 weeks ago"). |

### `check_toolchain`

Probe every catalogued scanner directly (its binary and version command; no bash needed) and report per-scanner status: installed, version, expected version floor, known-compromised releases (with the advisory id), the MCP tools that depend on it, and the suggested install command for this OS.

No parameters.

### `compliance_check`

(1) Trivy licence scan: risky licences, `licenses_summary`. (2) The offline rgpd.yml Semgrep pack: Portuguese personal identifiers (NIF, NISS, IBAN, phone, e-mail — by variable name) in logs, and trackers (GA4, Meta Pixel, Hotjar, YouTube) loaded before consent; accepting a Consent Mode v2 denial is a documented legal judgement. Heuristics, not proof. (3) `policy_documents_found`. A failed scanner lowers coverage; nothing for the pack to read is not applicable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |

### `compliance_evidence`

A Markdown evidence document from one project's recorded state: latest compliance scan, licences, CVE counts, baseline, suppressions, policy documents. framework gdpr, soc2, iso27001 or generic shapes the labels; owasp-top10-2025 and nist-csf-2.0 give per-category evidence, a category being covered only when, for every source language, a scanner that ran has rules for it. Reads history only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `framework` | one of "gdpr", "soc2", "iso27001", "owasp-top10-2025", "nist-csf-2.0", "generic" | no | — | gdpr, soc2, iso27001, generic (default), or owasp-top10-2025 / nist-csf-2.0 (per category). |

### `create_fix_pr`

Apply scanner-made fixes — deps\_update\_plan upgrades, the rules' own Semgrep autofixes — in a disposable worktree, verify them by re-running the scan and a test differential, and open one pull request per ecosystem or scanner. apply defaults to false: a dry run pushes nothing, but runs the project's own test command — the project's code, run as you. The repo's .npmrc/.yarnrc and like configs are set aside; a non-plain pip requirement, an npm network path or a Composer repository refuses the fix. `filtered` explains the rest.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Lowest severity to fix. Default high. |
| `sources` | array of one of "deps", "semgrep" | no | — | Which fix sources to consider. Default: both ('deps' and 'semgrep'). |
| `max_prs` | number | no | — | Pull requests per run, highest severity first; the rest in `deferred`. Default 3. |
| `apply` | boolean | no | — | true: commit, push, open the PRs. Default false: a dry run (still runs the test command). |

### `create_github_issues`

Open one GitHub issue per top open finding of project\_path with the local gh CLI and its existing login (never a suppressed finding). A finding with an issue in any state is skipped (its identity is in the title). severity\_min (default high) and max\_issues (default 10) cap the run; `filtered` and `filtered_reason` count what they dropped. Missing labels are created, or left off (`labels_omitted`). It files real issues unless dry\_run: preview first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Lowest severity filed. Default high; the rest are counted in `filtered`. |
| `max_issues` | number | no | — | Issues per run, highest severity first. Default 10. |
| `labels` | array of string | no | — | Labels for every issue. Default \["dev-guardian", "security"\]. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | — | true: list the issues without filing them. Default false. |

### `deps_audit`

Trivy fs plus the stack's own auditors: npm audit; pip-audit in a temporary virtualenv it installs the requirements into from PyPI (an sdist's build runs); for .NET, a locked restore and dotnet list package --vulnerable, which runs the project's MSBuild and contacts its NuGet feeds (an out-of-sync lock is a gap); for Go, govulncheck, which reports the vulnerable functions the code calls. Returns findings, indexed CVEs and `bot_configured` (Renovate or Dependabot).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Response floor only; every finding is still recorded (`severity_filter`). |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |

### `deps_update_plan`

Ordered upgrades from each stack's own outdated command (npm, composer, cargo, go, rubygems; dotnet after a locked restore, which runs MSBuild) and pip's own pins. Each entry: security (an active CVE in the latest deps scan; npm/pip target the minimum fixed version, other stacks the latest available), patch, minor or major, with its upgrade\_command; pnpm and yarn get overrides to apply by hand. `unplanned`: CVEs with no step, and why; `runner_failures`: commands that failed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `prefer` | one of "security", "patch", "minor", "major" | no | — | Sort entries so this classification appears first. Default: security. |

### `detect_stack`

Detect languages, package managers, frameworks, existing tools, IaC and CI, in-process. Manifests are read up to 3 directories deep (each also in `projects`); PHP and WordPress are detected without a composer.json. The snapshot is stored for the stack-aware tools.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |

### `diff_scans`

Compare two scans of a project and type. mode diff (default): new, resolved, unchanged and not\_remeasured findings (a type the newer scan did not measure — never resolved), matched by line-independent identity; from\_scan\_id / to\_scan\_id, else from (previous, baseline) to the latest. mode regression: the latest scan against its baseline (else the previous), weighted by severity; `regressed` past threshold. Suppressed findings count apart (summary.suppressed, suppressed\_findings, suppressed\_by\_severity); unmeasured ones in not\_remeasured\_by\_severity. Another project's scan id: unknown\_scan\_id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | one of "diff", "regression" | no | — | diff (default) or regression. |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `scan_type` | one of "security\_full", "sast", "secrets", "deps", "deps\_audit", "containers", "iac", "bugs", "quality", "review\_pr", "compliance", "audit", "sbom", "detect\_stack", "perf", "init", "observability", "wordpress", "wp\_audit", "wp\_vuln\_check", "wp\_vuln\_check\_source", "wp\_cron\_audit", "wp\_rest\_audit", "dotnet\_secrets", "dotnet\_target\_framework", "dotnet\_efcore\_audit", "skill\_audit", "dast", "agent\_audit", "mcp\_tool\_audit", "sarif\_import", "llm\_scan" | no | — | Compare scans of this type. Default: the newest finding-producing scan. |
| `source_tool` | string | no | — | sarif\_import only: the importing tool. Required when several were imported. |
| `from_scan_id` | string | no | — | The older side: this exact scan. Takes precedence over from. Default: see from. |
| `from` | one of "baseline", "previous" | no | — | The older side when from\_scan\_id is not given: previous (default) or baseline (set\_baseline's for that type). |
| `to_scan_id` | string | no | — | The newer side: this exact scan. Takes precedence over to. Default: see to. |
| `to` | one of "latest" | no | — | The newer side when to\_scan\_id is not given: latest (default). |
| `threshold` | number | no | — | regression: the weighted change that sets regressed. Default 5 (one new critical). |

### `dotnet_check`

One .NET check. secrets: appsettings\*.json, \*.config, nuget.config and launchSettings.json for what gitleaks misses — SQL Server connection strings, Azure keys, NuGet feed credentials, JWT signing keys. target\_framework: each project's TargetFramework (LTS, STS, end of life); no SDK needed. efcore: EF Core migrations that drop tables or columns, add NOT NULL without a default, or embed credentials. setup: the recorded .NET posture (these checks, NuGet CVEs, open findings), no scanner run.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `check` | one of "secrets", "target\_framework", "efcore", "setup" | yes | — | The check to run. |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |

### `export_vex`

Write a VEX document for the latest dependency scan, one statement per vulnerability and package version (by purl): not\_affected only from suppress\_finding with vex\_status; affected when validate\_finding finds the version imported by a route-reachable file; else under\_investigation, with the reason; never fixed. Writes .guardian/reports/vex-\*/; `unknowns` lists what it could not know; nothing is written when no vulnerability was measured. No network.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `format` | one of "openvex", "cyclonedx" | no | — | openvex (default) or cyclonedx (CycloneDX 1.6). |
| `author` | string | no | — | Who makes the statements. Default "Unknown Author". |

### `generate_sbom`

Produce a CycloneDX or SPDX JSON SBOM with Syft (Trivy as fallback), always written to .guardian/reports/sbom-&lt;scan&gt;/ (`file_path`). The response inlines it when it is at most inline\_max\_kb (default 64 KB); `inlined` says whether it did.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `format` | one of "cyclonedx-json", "spdx-json" | no | — | SBOM output format. Default: cyclonedx-json. |
| `inline_max_kb` | number | no | — | Inline the SBOM when it is at most this many KB (0 never; at most 1024). Default 64. |

### `health_status`

Server uptime, database, shell, in-flight scans, tool counts and one project's last scan. `storage_warning` (null when fine): the project's .guardian/guardian.db is not used (a copy, or not registered) and history goes to a per-user fallback — tell the user to run the `db adopt` command it names in their own terminal; never run it yourself. `suppressions` {active, this\_project, all\_projects}: all\_projects ones hide findings in every project. `storage.future_dated_scans_ignored`, `future_dated_note`: future-dated scans, which every count ignores.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |

### `import_sarif`

Import another tool's SARIF 2.1.0 log (CodeQL, Snyk, …) into the history: one sarif\_import scan per run, named by its tool, whose findings then work in set\_baseline, diff\_scans, suppress\_finding, prioritize\_findings and report\_export (source\_tool picks the tool). Results that are not findings, or were suppressed at the source, are counted, not imported. Nothing the log names is opened or run. The log: a file of at most 50 MiB under project\_path, unless allow\_outside\_project.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `sarif_path` | string | yes | — | The SARIF 2.1.0 log to import: absolute, or relative to project\_path. |
| `allow_outside_project` | boolean | no | — | Read a log outside project\_path. Default false. |
| `max_results` | number | no | — | Results imported before stopping (the scan is then partial). Default 50000. |

### `init_project`

Install the gitleaks, Renovate, Semgrep and pre-commit configs (profile minimal, standard or paranoid) and report a first secrets, vulnerability and SAST status. refresh compares your copies with the current ones: apply false only reports; apply true updates the files you never edited and writes &lt;name&gt;.new beside the others — an edited file is never overwritten.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `profile` | one of "minimal", "standard", "paranoid" | no | — | minimal (gitleaks, Renovate), standard (+ Semgrep, pre-commit) or paranoid (stricter). Default standard. |
| `apply` | boolean | no | — | When false, return only the proposed file list without writing. Default: true. |
| `refresh` | boolean | no | — | Compare installed configs with the current ones; writes only with apply, never over your edits. |

### `install_toolchain`

Install missing scanners — the standard set, or `tools` — with the install scripts (Linux, macOS) or winget, scoop, choco or WSL (Windows). Syft, Trivy and gitleaks come at a pinned version (a release checked against its sha256 goes to ~/.local/bin); `binary_path` and `path_note` say where each went. This changes the system: run dry\_run first, which only lists the commands.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tools` | array of string | no | — | Install only these catalogued scanners. Default: the standard set for the stack. |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | — | Print commands without executing. Default: false. |
| `elevation_allowed` | boolean | no | — | Allow steps that need sudo or admin (else listed in `requires_elevation`). |

### `license_compatibility`

Check the project's licence (package.json, pyproject.toml, composer.json, .csproj or LICENSE) against its dependencies' licences from this project's latest compliance\_check. No declared licence, or a proprietary label, counts as proprietary and still flags copyleft; an unrecognised or compound SPDX expression on either side is `undetermined`, never compatible. Reads history only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |

### `llm_scan`

Your model verifies the scanners' findings and hunts what they miss; the server calls no model. step start: plan it, modes verify (a task per finding with a file and line) or hunt (needs map\_attack\_surface); returns plan\_id and a token estimate. Above max\_estimated\_tokens nothing is handed out until confirm: true, which the user must agree to. step task: lease the next task; its brief goes to a fresh subagent, one per task; done: true and the report at the end. step submit: that task's answer as payload; an invalid one is refused with the reasons, two more tries.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `step` | one of "start", "task", "submit" | yes | — | start: plan (with plan\_id: its report). task {plan\_id}: lease the next task. submit {plan\_id, task\_id, lease\_token, independence, payload}: that task's answer. |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `modes` | array of one of "verify", "hunt" | no | — | verify checks scanner findings; hunt looks for what they miss. Default \[verify\]. |
| `scan_id` | string | no | — | Verify the findings of this scan. Default: the project open set. |
| `fingerprints` | array of string | no | — | Verify only these findings. |
| `max_tasks` | number | no | — | Stop handing out tasks after this many. Default 200. |
| `max_estimated_tokens` | number | no | — | Above this estimate the plan needs confirm: true. Default 500000. |
| `per_task_overhead` | number | no | — | Host tokens assumed per task. Default 60000. |
| `confirm` | boolean | no | — | Accept an estimate above the limit. |
| `plan_id` | string | no | — | task, submit: the plan step start returned. start: report on this plan instead of planning (confirm: true confirms it). |
| `execute` | one of "host", "sampling" | no | — | host (default): hand the task out. sampling: run it through the client's MCP sampling. |
| `task_id` | string | no | — | submit: the task, as step task returned it. |
| `lease_token` | string | no | — | submit: the lease\_token step task returned with the task. |
| `independence` | one of "subagent", "same\_context" | no | — | subagent: a fresh context ran the brief; same\_context: you did (never demotes or confirms). |
| `payload` | unknown | no | — | submit: the answer, matching the task's response\_schema. At most 64 KiB serialized. |

### `map_attack_surface`

Statically extract the reachable surface — HTTP routes (method, path, params), environment variables read, container ports — across the supported stacks, and diff OpenAPI 3 / Swagger 2 documents against the routes: shadow endpoints and dead documentation. Stores a snapshot (guardian://surface/latest has the full route list) and returns a summary with samples. scan\_dast and validate\_finding need it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |
| `include_env_vars` | boolean | no | `true` | Collect environment-variable names the code reads. Default: true. |
| `spec_paths` | array of string | no | — | OpenAPI / Swagger documents to read instead of discovering them. |

### `observability_setup`

Propose stack-appropriate observability files (Pino logger / structlog / Monolog, plus a Prometheus-compatible metrics module). When apply=true (default false), writes the files; otherwise returns proposals only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `apply` | boolean | no | — | When true, write the proposed files to disk. Default: false (dry-run). |

### `perf_check`

Run Lighthouse against target\_url, or k6 against k6\_script\_path: Core Web Vitals, or request counts and p95/p99, and the raw report's path. Lighthouse runs are checked against .guardian/budgets.yml: an exceeded budget is a finding, and `budgets.status` never reads an unmeasured metric as within budget. Sends real load to the URL.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `target_url` | string | no | — | URL to probe with Lighthouse. Mutually exclusive with k6\_script\_path. |
| `k6_script_path` | string | no | — | Path to a k6 script to execute. Mutually exclusive with target\_url. |
| `lighthouse_categories` | array of one of "performance", "accessibility", "best-practices", "seo", "pwa" | no | — | Categories to include. Default: all five. |

### `precommit_install`

Run `pre-commit install` in the project to wire its .pre-commit-config.yaml into git hooks. Requires pre-commit on PATH (install via install\_toolchain).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |

### `prioritize_findings`

One project's open findings (newest usable scan of each type, suppressions out). view rank (default): by severity, category, fix availability and age, boosted for CVEs on CISA KEV or with a high EPSS, each CVE with a CISA SSVC decision (Act, Attend, Track\*, Track); missing data is named, never invented. view triage: likely\_false\_positive, probably\_safe or keep, from paths (tests, generated code, fixtures) — suppress\_finding candidates for you to judge.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `view` | one of "rank", "triage" | no | — | rank (default) or triage. |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `limit` | number | no | — | rank: how many to return, 1–500. Default 50. |
| `mission_wellbeing` | one of "low", "medium", "high" | no | — | rank: SSVC Mission & Well-being of this system. Default medium. |

### `quality_check`

jscpd duplication (any language), ruff and radon complexity for Python, ESLint when configured and installed in node\_modules (it runs the project's config), staticcheck for Go, shellcheck for shell scripts, detekt for Kotlin and RuboCop for Ruby (on Java and Ruby). Findings: duplicate, complexity, smell or naming; `categories` filters the response, not the scan. A missing or failed analyser makes coverage partial. Budgets exceeded in .guardian/budgets.yml are findings (not with scope).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `categories` | array of one of "duplicate", "complexity", "smell", "naming" | no | — | Show only these classes; every finding is still recorded (`category_filter`). |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |
| `scope` | object | no | — | Scan part of the project: paths, a git change set, or changes since a ref or date. Never a baseline. |
| `scope.paths` | array of string | no | — | Files, directories or globs in project\_path; with diff or since, narrows that set. |
| `scope.diff` | object | no | — | A git change set. {} = every uncommitted change (staged, unstaged, untracked). |
| `scope.diff.base` | string | no | — | The files changed since the merge base of this ref and head. |
| `scope.diff.head` | string | no | — | Must be the checked-out commit. Default HEAD. |
| `scope.diff.staged` | boolean | no | — | Only the staged files. |
| `scope.diff.include_untracked` | boolean | no | — | Also untracked files. Default: true without base or staged. |
| `scope.since` | string | no | — | What changed since a commit, tag or date ("2 weeks ago"). |

### `register_custom_rules`

Register Semgrep rule files for this project (paths, or found in .semgrep/, semgrep/, rules/); scan\_sast and bug\_hunt then run them. Each must be a valid rules file and, when Semgrep is installed, pass semgrep --validate; anything else is returned in `rejected` with the reason, never registered. A registered file that later disappears or breaks is skipped, not fatal. clear removes the registration.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `paths` | array of string | no | — | Rule files, directories or globs. Default: .semgrep/, semgrep/ and rules/. |
| `clear` | boolean | no | — | Remove this project's registered rules. |

### `report_export`

Write a scan report as markdown (default), html (self-contained, light/dark), sarif (SARIF 2.1.0, CWE and OWASP Top 10:2025 tags) or json, saying which OWASP categories the scan tested; content\_markdown renders a narrative instead. An explicit scan\_id must be one of project\_path's (another project's is refused, with retry\_with naming its project) and not still running. source\_tool: that tool's newest SARIF import.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `scan_id` | string | no | — | Scan to export. Default: project\_path's newest usable scan. |
| `source_tool` | string | no | — | Without scan\_id: export this tool's newest SARIF import. |
| `format` | one of "html", "sarif", "markdown", "json" | no | `"markdown"` | markdown (default), html (self-contained, light/dark), sarif (SARIF 2.1.0) or json. |
| `content_markdown` | string | no | — | A Markdown narrative to render instead of a scan (scan\_id is then ignored). |
| `title` | string | no | — | Title for the content\_markdown report. Default: "Pro Digital Key — Report". |
| `subtitle` | string | no | — | Optional subtitle under the title (content\_markdown mode). |
| `lang` | one of "en", "pt", "es" | no | — | Language for the HTML shell chrome (report title + footer). Default: en. |

### `review_pr`

Scan a branch's changes between base\_ref and head\_ref: Semgrep (scan\_sast's rules), Bandit, gosec and cppcheck on changed files, gitleaks on those commits (and uncommitted files when head is checked out), Trivy when a manifest changed. An unresolvable ref is an error, never "no files changed". `preexisting_manifest_gaps`: manifests Trivy could not read that the diff did not touch — the project's gap, not the review's.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `base_ref` | string | no | — | Base ref for the diff. Defaults to origin/HEAD, then main, then master. |
| `head_ref` | string | no | — | Head ref. Defaults to HEAD. |
| `local_only` | boolean | no | — | Semgrep with rules on disk only (the project's, registered, the plugin's LLM, web-JS and mobile packs). Trivy may still go out. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Response floor only; every finding is still recorded (`severity_filter`). |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |

### `risk_score`

A 0-100 risk score and band for one project from its recorded scans, open findings (newest usable scan of each type, suppressions out), CVEs (weighted up for CISA KEV or a high EPSS) and baseline, with the breakdown, the next action and `coverage` (`coverage_caveat` when incomplete). `suppressed_count`: what suppressions took out — a mass suppression is never a clean project. `future_dated_note`: future-dated scans ignored.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |

### `sbom_diff`

Compare two generate\_sbom scans of project\_path (default: its two latest): components added, removed and changed, keyed by ecosystem and name with every version kept. Refuses to compare a full list with a capped summary; the response arrays are capped, `summary` has the true totals.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `from_scan_id` | string | no | — | The older SBOM scan. Default: the second-newest. |

| `use_full_file` | boolean | no | — | Ignored; kept for old callers. |

### `scan_containers`

Trivy on a Dockerfile (config) and/or an image (vulnerabilities, secrets, misconfiguration); with neither, ./Dockerfile. hadolint lints the Dockerfile; a root compose file is checked for privileged containers, host networking, docker.sock and unpinned tags. An image's Sigstore signature is checked with cosign: a real verify with signer\_identity and signer\_issuer (a rejection is high), else whether a signature and SLSA provenance exist. A registry failure is unknown, never absent.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Response floor only; every finding is still recorded (`severity_filter`). |
| `dockerfile_path` | string | no | — | Path to a Dockerfile to scan with `trivy config`. |
| `image` | string | no | — | Container image reference to scan with `trivy image`. |
| `signer_identity` | string | no | — | The identity `image` must be signed by (a workflow URL or an e-mail). Needs signer\_issuer. |
| `signer_identity_regexp` | string | no | — | signer\_identity as an RE2 regular expression. |
| `signer_issuer` | string | no | — | The OIDC issuer of that identity, e.g. `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`. |
| `signer_issuer_regexp` | string | no | — | signer\_issuer as a regular expression (Go RE2 syntax). Not with signer\_issuer. |
| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |

### `scan_dast`

Send real HTTP requests to an already-running application along the latest map\_attack\_surface inventory (none: no\_surface\_snapshot): reachability, anonymous access to auth-required routes, authorization differences, CORS, headers, information disclosure, methods, open redirects; nuclei and a rate-limit burst are opt-in. Loopback only unless the user attests authorized\_target; read-only methods unless allow\_write\_methods. No injection payloads: a clean result is no proof of injection safety.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `base_url` | string | yes | — | Origin of the running application, e.g. `http://localhost:3000`. |
| `authorized_target` | boolean | no | — | The user's attestation that they may scan this non-loopback host. Never set it on their behalf. |
| `allow_write_methods` | boolean | no | — | Allow POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE probes, with an empty body. Default false. |
| `probe_rate_limit` | boolean | no | — | Send one bounded burst with a fake credential to one login endpoint. Default false. |
| `rate_limit_path` | string | no | — | Inventory path to aim the rate-limit burst at. Default: inferred from auth-shaped paths. |
| `auth_header_env` | string | no | — | Name of an environment variable holding the Authorization header; the secret stays out of the conversation. |
| `auth_header` | string | no | — | Literal Authorization header: it lands in the transcript, so prefer auth\_header\_env. |
| `use_nuclei` | boolean | no | — | Also run nuclei against the origin (not these routes). Default false. |
| `max_requests` | number | no | — | Global request ceiling. Default: 750. Reported when it cuts. |
| `timeout_ms` | number | no | — | Per-request timeout in milliseconds. Default: 5000. |
| `wall_clock_ms` | number | no | — | Ceiling on the whole probing phase, in ms. Default 600000. |

### `scan_deps`

Trivy fs over the project's manifests and lock files: each finding with its CVE, severity and fixed version. `packages` narrows the response, not the scan. A manifest Trivy cannot read is a named gap. The project's .trivyignore is honoured (`tools_run[].honoured_config`); `suppressed_by_repo_config` names what it suppressed — reported, not findings.

| `force` | boolean | no | `false` | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |
| `packages` | array of string | no | — | Show only these packages' findings; the scan records all (`package_filter`). |

A history pass over 0 commits is failed, never clean. | `scope` | object | no | — | Scan part of the project: paths, a git change set, or changes since a ref or date. Never a baseline. |
| `scope.paths` | array of string | no | — | Files, directories or globs in project\_path; with diff or since, narrows that set. |
| `scope.diff` | object | no | — | A git change set. {} = every uncommitted change (staged, unstaged, untracked). |
| `scope.diff.base` | string | no | — | The files changed since the merge base of this ref and head. |
| `scope.diff.head` | string | no | — | Must be the checked-out commit. Default HEAD. |
| `scope.diff.staged` | boolean | no | — | Only the staged files. |
| `scope.diff.include_untracked` | boolean | no | — | Also untracked files. Default: true without base or staged. |
| `scope.since` | string | no | — | What changed since a commit, tag or date ("2 weeks ago"). |
| `verify_live` | boolean | no | `false` | Ask each secret's own provider whether it is live: sends the secrets out, so ask the user first. |

Audit a third-party AI skill, MCP server, plugin or agent before installing it (a directory, file, .zip or git/HTTP(S) URL): prompt injection, exfiltration, privilege escalation, excessive agency, tool poisoning, dangerous code, taint flows — the commands in instruction files and hook / plugin / MCP configs scored like scripts — and OSV CVEs of its dependencies. For sarif\_import, source\_tool picks the tool. To accept one reviewed finding, suppress it instead.

| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `scan_id` | string | no | — | Scan to mark as the baseline. Defaults to project\_path's newest usable scan. |
| `scan_type` | one of "security\_full", "sast", "secrets", "deps", "deps\_audit", "containers", "iac", "bugs", "quality", "review\_pr", "compliance", "audit", "sbom", "detect\_stack", "perf", "init", "observability", "wordpress", "wp\_audit", "wp\_vuln\_check", "wp\_vuln\_check\_source", "wp\_cron\_audit", "wp\_rest\_audit", "dotnet\_secrets", "dotnet\_target\_framework", "dotnet\_efcore\_audit", "skill\_audit", "dast", "agent\_audit", "mcp\_tool\_audit", "sarif\_import", "llm\_scan" | no | — | Without scan\_id: baseline the newest scan of this type. |
| `source_tool` | string | no | — | sarif\_import only: the importing tool. Required when several were imported. |
| `note` | string | no | — | Free-form note attached to the baseline row. |

### `suggest_fix`

Gather a finding's context — the source around it, rule metadata, earlier suppressions of the same rule — from project\_path's newest scan that reported it, so you can write the patch. Calls no LLM. A line that holds a secret (a credential finding, or the secret detector) is withheld and named in redacted\_lines.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `finding_fingerprint` | string | yes | — | Fingerprint of the finding to gather context for. |
| `context_lines` | number | no | — | How many lines of source context to include around the finding. Default 20. |

### `suppress_finding`

Mark a finding (by the fingerprint a scan showed) as a false positive; it stays hidden after the code moves. A fingerprint no scan of this project reported is `unknown_finding`. expires\_at snoozes. For a finding with its own CVE, GHSA or PYSEC id and a package version, vex\_status: not\_affected with a justification also makes a VEX statement (export\_vex); the reply names other open copies of the vulnerability.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `finding_fingerprint` | string | yes | — | SHA-256 fingerprint of the finding to suppress (from a previous scan response). |
| `reason` | string | yes | — | Why this finding is being suppressed. Required. |
| `expires_at` | string | no | — | ISO-8601 expiry. When omitted, the suppression never expires. |
| `vex_status` | one of "not\_affected" | no | — | Also record a VEX not\_affected statement for the finding's vulnerability. Needs justification. |
| `justification` | one of "component\_not\_present", "vulnerable\_code\_not\_present", "vulnerable\_code\_not\_in\_execute\_path", "vulnerable\_code\_cannot\_be\_controlled\_by\_adversary", "inline\_mitigations\_already\_exist" | no | — | OpenVEX justification for vex\_status not\_affected. Required with it. |
| `impact_statement` | string | no | — | Optional free-text VEX impact statement, with vex\_status. |

### `validate_finding`

Per open finding: does a file an HTTP route reaches import its file (static) or, for a dependency CVE, its package (dependency)? reachable, unreachable or unknown, with evidence. Needs map\_attack\_surface. Report only: it never suppresses a finding or changes a severity. The unit is the file; Ruby, Java, C# and PHP never get unreachable; nothing detects a dynamic import, so where one is used unreachable can be wrong and this tool cannot tell you when.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `fingerprint` | string | no | — | Validate only this finding. Default: every open finding. |
| `finding_fingerprint` | string | no | — | Same as fingerprint (the name other tools use); pass one. |
| `providers` | array of one of "static", "dependency" | no | — | static (the finding's file) and/or dependency (a CVE's package). Default: both. |

### `vet_packages`

Check packages before installing them, against the registry and OSV: the name exists (unpublished: likely hallucinated), the version is not malicious, known vulnerabilities, publish age (under 72 h warns), npm install scripts, typosquatting. Verdict per package: block, warn, unknown or ok — unknown means a check could not run, never ok. Accepts name or name@version. Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ecosystem` | one of "npm", "pnpm", "yarn", "bun", "pypi", "pip", "python", "uv", "poetry", "packagist", "composer", "php", "nuget", "dotnet" | yes | — | npm (also pnpm/yarn/bun), pypi (pip/uv/poetry), packagist (composer) or nuget (dotnet). |
| `packages` | array of string | yes | — | Package specs: "name" or "name@version". |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | The project whose registry configuration applies. Default: the server's working directory. |

### `wp_audit`

Audit a WordPress install with WP-CLI, changing nothing. mode install (default): core and plugin checksums (themes: not checked), administrators with risky logins, DISALLOW\_FILE\_EDIT / WP\_DEBUG / FORCE\_SSL\_ADMIN, auto-updating plugins. mode cron: scheduled events with unknown hooks, base64-looking arguments or an inactive plugin — where backdoors persist. mode bulk: the install audit of up to 50 installs. Needs WP-CLI; checksums come from api.wordpress.org. WP-CLI boots the site with its plugins and theme skipped; wp-config.php, core files and must-use plugins still run.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | one of "install", "cron", "bulk" | no | — | install (default), cron or bulk. |
| `wp_install_path` | string | no | — | install, cron: the directory holding wp-config.php. |
| `include_users` | boolean | no | — | install: list the administrators, flagging risky logins. Default true. |
| `include_options` | boolean | no | — | install: read the config flags. Default true. |
| `risky_login_names` | array of string | no | — | install: logins to flag, replacing the default list. |
| `wp_install_paths` | array of string | no | — | bulk: up to 50 install directories. |
| `concurrency` | number | no | — | bulk: installs audited at once, 1–10. Default 4. |

### `wp_report`

What dev-guardian recorded about one WordPress install (project\_path = its root); no service queried. kind setup: the latest install, cron and REST audits (target\_url for those keyed by URL), open WordPress findings, CVEs. kind hardening: a prioritised checklist from the latest install audit. kind plugin: one slug's recorded CVEs and, with a local wp\_install\_path, its version and state from WP-CLI, which boots the site (its database; its PHP minus plugins and theme). Run wp\_audit or wp\_vuln\_check first for fresh data.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | one of "setup", "hardening", "plugin" | yes | — | setup, hardening or plugin. |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `target_url` | string | no | — | setup, plugin: the site URL its scans were recorded under (nothing is sent). |
| `slug` | string | no | — | plugin: the wp.org slug, e.g. "contact-form-7". |
| `wp_install_path` | string | no | — | plugin: a local install; WP-CLI reads the plugin's version and state. |

### `wp_vuln_check`

Known WordPress vulnerabilities and exposure. mode live (default): WPScan against target\_url (or a local install's URL) for core, plugin and theme CVEs; with no API token it reads not checked, never clean. mode source: a local install's versions (project\_path = the install root) against the Wordfence feed (WORDFENCE\_API\_KEY; without it, partial) and wp.org (closed or stale plugins). mode rest: GET probes of the live REST API — users, drafts, comments, xmlrpc.php.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | one of "live", "source", "rest" | no | — | live (default), source or rest. |
| `wp_install_path` | string | no | — | live: a local install whose wp-config.php gives the URL. |
| `target_url` | string | no | — | live, rest: the live site's URL. |
| `api_token` | string | no | — | WPScan API token. Falls back to WPSCAN\_API\_TOKEN env var. |
| `project_path` | string | no | — | Project root. Default: the server's working directory. |
| `severity_min` | one of "info", "low", "medium", "high", "critical" | no | — | Response floor only; every finding is still recorded (`severity_filter`). |
| `force` | boolean | no | — | Bypass the tree-hash cache. |
| `timeout_ms` | number | no | — | rest: per-request timeout, 1000–60000 ms. Default 15000. |

## Hidden aliases

Each of these names still answers `tools/call` with its own parameters, but `tools/list` does not show it: the listed tool runs it, with the same parameters, as one of its modes.

A host permission matches the name that is called. A rule written for an alias (Claude Code: `mcp__plugin_dev-guardian_dev-guardian__wp_rest_audit`) does not apply to its fold call (`wp_vuln_check { mode: "rest" }`), which is what a model calls now. Write the rule for the listed name (`mcp__plugin_dev-guardian_dev-guardian__wp_vuln_check`): it covers every mode of the fold, since a permission cannot tell one mode's arguments from another's. Keep the alias's own rule as well, for anything that still calls the alias directly.

| Name | Listed as |
| --- | --- |
| `bulk_audit_wordpress_sites` | `wp_audit { mode: "bulk" }` |
| `dotnet_describe_setup` | `dotnet_check { check: "setup" }` |
| `dotnet_efcore_audit` | `dotnet_check { check: "efcore" }` |
| `dotnet_target_framework_check` | `dotnet_check { check: "target_framework" }` |
| `llm_scan_start` | `llm_scan { step: "start" }` |
| `llm_scan_submit` | `llm_scan { step: "submit" }` |
| `llm_scan_task` | `llm_scan { step: "task" }` |
| `regression_alert` | `diff_scans { mode: "regression" }` |
| `scan_dotnet_secrets` | `dotnet_check { check: "secrets" }` |
| `triage_findings` | `prioritize_findings { view: "triage" }` |
| `wp_cron_audit` | `wp_audit { mode: "cron" }` |
| `wp_describe_setup` | `wp_report { kind: "setup" }` |
| `wp_plugin_check` | `wp_report { kind: "plugin" }` |
| `wp_recommend_hardening` | `wp_report { kind: "hardening" }` |
| `wp_rest_audit` | `wp_vuln_check { mode: "rest" }` |
| `wp_vuln_check_source` | `wp_vuln_check { mode: "source" }` |

## Resources

Every resource returns compact JSON and answers for the project the server was started in.

| URI | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `guardian://baseline` | `guardian-baseline` | Active regression baseline of the server's working-directory project: `{ baseline_id, scan_id, scan_type, set_at, note? }` — never another project's. Returns `{ active: false }` when this project has no baseline. |
| `guardian://compliance/status` | `guardian-compliance-status` | Compliance status of the server's working-directory project from its most recent compliance\_check: licenses\_summary, risky\_licenses, and policy\_documents\_found. Returns `{ last_run: null }` when no compliance scan exists. |
| `guardian://cves/active` | `guardian-cves-active` | CVEs of the server's working-directory project, from its newest deps-flavoured scan (deps / deps\_audit / security\_full) that actually ran a dependency scanner, each with `kev`/`epss_score`/`epss_percentile` when already cached (cache only — call prioritize\_findings or risk\_score first to refresh). Returns `{ cves: [] }` when no deps scan has run. |
| `guardian://dotnet/efcore` | `guardian-dotnet-efcore` | Latest dotnet\_check {check: "efcore"}: dangerous migration patterns detected (DropTable, DropColumn, AlterColumn nullable=false without defaultValue, raw SQL with credentials). |
| `guardian://dotnet/target-frameworks` | `guardian-dotnet-target-frameworks` | Latest dotnet\_check {check: "target\_framework"}: per-project target framework moniker + EOL/legacy status. |
| `guardian://findings/by-severity/{level}{?page,page_size}` | `guardian-findings-by-severity` | Open findings of one severity (info \| low \| medium \| high \| critical). Scoped to the server's working-directory project: the newest usable scan of every finding-producing type (never an SBOM, stack detection or diff review; a scan whose scanners did not run is skipped — `skipped` counts them and names the newest few), deduplicated, active suppressions removed. Paged with ?page=N&page\_size=M (default 50, max 100); messages are cut to 500 characters. |
| `guardian://findings/critical{?page,page_size}` | `guardian-findings-critical` | Open findings with severity=critical. Scoped to the server's working-directory project: the newest usable scan of every finding-producing type (never an SBOM, stack detection or diff review; a scan whose scanners did not run is skipped — `skipped` counts them and names the newest few), deduplicated, active suppressions removed. Paged with ?page=N&page\_size=M (default 50, max 100); messages are cut to 500 characters. |
| `guardian://findings/open{?page,page_size}` | `guardian-findings-open` | All open findings. Scoped to the server's working-directory project: the newest usable scan of every finding-producing type (never an SBOM, stack detection or diff review; a scan whose scanners did not run is skipped — `skipped` counts them and names the newest few), deduplicated, active suppressions removed. Paged with ?page=N&page\_size=M (default 50, max 100); messages are cut to 500 characters. |
| `guardian://sbom` | `guardian-sbom` | Metadata for the server's working-directory project's most recent SBOM produced by `generate_sbom`: format, produced\_by, file path on disk, component count, top packages. Inline payload omitted — read the file or call generate\_sbom for the full document. |
| `guardian://scans/{scan_id}` | `guardian-scans-by-id` | Full ScanResult for a given scan\_id (record + findings counts + top\_findings). Returns an MCP error (-32602) if the id is unknown. |
| `guardian://scans/history` | `guardian-scans-history` | Up to 50 most-recent scans of the server's working-directory project, across every type, ordered by start time descending. Records are sparse — call `guardian://scans/{scan_id}` for the full ScanResult. |
| `guardian://scans/latest` | `guardian-scans-latest` | Latest completed scan of any type of the server's working-directory project, with severity counts and the top-10 findings inlined. Returns `{ last_run: null }` when no scan has run yet. For what is open across every scan type, read guardian://findings/open. |
| `guardian://stack` | `guardian-stack` | Latest stack snapshot of the server's working-directory project, produced by `detect_stack`. Returns `{ snapshot: null }` when no snapshot exists yet. |
| `guardian://surface/{id}` | `guardian-surface-by-id` | A specific attack-surface snapshot of the server's working-directory project by id, as returned in `snapshot_id` by `map_attack_surface`, in full. Returns `{ snapshot: null }` for an unknown id or another project's snapshot. |
| `guardian://surface/latest` | `guardian-surface-latest` | Latest attack-surface snapshot of the server's working-directory project, from `map_attack_surface`: routes (code- and spec-provenance) with resolved path, method, params and auth hint, env vars, declared ports, per-language coverage, spec\_files and the spec\_diff (matched, code\_only, spec\_only, unmatchable). Each list is capped at 200 entries — `totals` has the true counts, `truncated` names what was cut, and guardian://surface/{snapshot\_id} returns the whole snapshot. Import edges and third-party imports are counted, not inlined. Returns `{ snapshot: null }` when none exists yet. |
| `guardian://wp/audit/{scan_id}` | `guardian-wp-audit-by-id` | wp\_audit result for a specific scan\_id. Errors -32602 when the id is unknown or is not a wp\_audit scan. |
| `guardian://wp/audit/latest` | `guardian-wp-audit-latest` | Most recent wp\_audit result: WP version, file checksum mismatches, config flags, admin users, plugins with auto\_update. Returns `{ last_run: null }` when no audit exists. |
| `guardian://wp/cron` | `guardian-wp-cron` | Latest wp\_audit {mode: "cron"} result: total scheduled events + flagged ones (suspicious hooks, base64-looking args, hooks from inactive plugins). |
